questions.question: Several agent applications duplicate definitions for the same tools. Each tool change requires edits in every application. What role does MCP play in the lesson?

options.text: Provide a standard way to expose and connect reusable tools through client-server separation.

questions.question: A course-writing agent must research before drafting. Independent factual and style reviews may run together, but a human must approve publication. Which workflow choices fit?

options.text: Run the independent reviews in parallel after drafting.
options.explanation: Independent checks can run concurrently once their shared input exists.

options.text: Publish in parallel with research before a draft or approval exists.
options.explanation: Publication depends on a completed, approved draft and cannot safely precede those inputs.

options.text: Insert a human-in-the-loop approval stage before publication.
options.explanation: The workflow must implement the stated requirement for human approval.

questions.takeaway: Choose workflow patterns from actual dependencies and approval requirements.

questions.question: An agent’s final answers fail after long sessions. Investigation suggests either lost user preferences or bad tool decisions. Which actions help isolate and repair these failures?

options.text: Evaluate memory retrieval and tool-selection components separately.
options.explanation: Component-level evaluation identifies where the end-to-end result goes wrong.

options.text: Ask the agent to praise its own final answer and treat that as verification.
options.explanation: Unstructured self-approval gives no reliable external evidence of correctness.

options.text: Test a rolling summary or retrieval-based memory against preference-retention cases.
options.explanation: The lesson’s memory strategies address limits of keeping or truncating raw conversation history; evaluation checks the trade-off.

options.text: Use actual tool results as feedback and rerun representative end-to-end tasks.
options.explanation: External feedback can ground reflection, and end-to-end evaluation confirms the combined system still serves the user.

questions.takeaway: Isolate failing components, ground checks in evidence, and confirm improvements on complete tasks.
